name: Google Ads Performance Coach
value_proposition: Before any budget move, check whether the primary conversion is a qualified outcome, then show period changes with visible formulas and an evidence-labelled list the owner verifies — the Blueprint never edits Google Ads.
persona: An owner, marketer, or consultant who already runs Google Ads and can export reports, but does not know which number to trust before changing a budget.
problem: Ad spend decisions are made on conversion numbers that may not measure a qualified outcome. A generic chatbot will happily optimize the wrong conversion.
workflow: 1. The person writes the qualified outcome for this business (for example form_submit = completed contact form) and lists events that do not count (default: page_view, add_to_cart). PERSON DECIDES: what a conversion must mean before any number is trusted.

2. The person exports the current and previous Google Ads campaign reports as CSV (campaign, clicks, cost, conversions, primary_conversion, plus each file's date range), a conversion-actions screenshot or table from Goals > Conversions > Summary, GA4 Traffic acquisition and Landing page exports for the same two ranges, and a search-terms export when the campaign type provides one. PERSON DECIDES: which columns to keep. Remove customer emails and other columns the workflow does not need.

3. The person checks the data settings of their AI assistant (chat history, training use, and file retention) before pasting or uploading anything. File upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings. PERSON DECIDES: whether to upload the files, paste the rows as text, or not use AI for this data at all.

4. The person pastes the Measurement Review Prompt and their rules from the Qualified Outcome Worksheet, then attaches or pastes the conversion-actions table, the campaign exports, and the GA4 landing-page rows.

5. AI runs the measurement check first. For each in-scope campaign it compares primary_conversion to the owner's qualified outcome. If the primary conversion is not a qualified outcome, or the conversion-actions table is missing, AI stops efficiency ranking for that campaign, writes MEASUREMENT REVIEW FIRST, and does not recommend bid, budget, status, or targeting changes.

6. For campaigns that pass the measurement check, AI fills the calculation workbook using only export numbers and leaves every formula visible (cost / conversions, current minus previous). Campaigns that failed measurement may show the same formula labelled not meaningful; that figure is never used to rank spend. Google Ads conversions and GA4 events are listed as separate CONFIRMED counts and are not forced to match.

7. AI labels each point as CONFIRMED (from an export or the conversion-actions table), AI INTERPRETATION (a possible explanation), or RECOMMENDED ACTION. It does not invent clicks, cost, conversions, savings, or ROI. PERSON DECIDES: whether each recommended action happens.

8. The person uses the Action Review Checklist and checks every CONFIRMED number against the export row before touching Google Ads. PERSON DECIDES: whether to change a primary conversion, wait and re-export, or change nothing. The person makes any change in Google Ads themselves. The Blueprint never edits the account.
before: The owner compares two dashboards by hand, trusts the conversion count, and moves budget on a hunch.
after: The owner knows whether the numbers can be trusted, sees calculated changes with visible formulas, and gets a short evidence-labelled list of what to verify next.

guided_demo.summary: A public, six-step walkthrough at /blueprints/google-ads-performance-coach using a fictional two-campaign Google Ads account dated 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30, with a previous period of 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-31 and no live Google Ads or GA4 connection. The qualified outcome is form_submit. Spring Promo fails the measurement check because its primary conversion is page_view; the demo stops efficiency ranking there, shows one CONFIRMED finding and one AI INTERPRETATION, shows Brand's workbook formula only because form_submit matches, and states that every number is invented. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled with text, not color alone.
steps: Step 1 of 6 - The exports: show the fictional current campaign table (Spring Promo, Brand), the previous-period table (same two campaigns), the conversion-actions table (page_view primary for Spring Promo, form_submit primary for Brand), and the GA4 landing-page table (/spring-landing, /contact). Show the qualified outcome text 'form_submit (completed contact form)', current_period '2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30', and previous_period '2026-08-01 to 2026-08-31'. Label the tables invented. State that no live Google Ads or GA4 account is attached.

Step 2 of 6 - Measurement review first: show the exact heading 'MEASUREMENT REVIEW FIRST'. List Spring Promo as failed because primary_conversion is page_view, not form_submit, with CONFIRMED text containing 'page_view', '96', and '12'. List Brand as passed because primary_conversion is form_submit. State that Spring Promo is skipped for efficiency ranking.

Step 3 of 6 - Visible formulas, then stop: show a workbook table. Spring Promo formula text '=1860/96', result '19.38', meaningful 'no'. Brand formula text '=290/22', result '13.18', meaningful 'yes'. Show the text labels 'CONFIRMED', 'AI INTERPRETATION', and 'RECOMMENDED ACTION' as visible words, not as color or icon alone. Show AI INTERPRETATION text containing 'not meaningful until tracking changes'. Show RECOMMENDED ACTION text containing 'Do not change bids yet'.

Step 4 of 6 - Check the facts: open the Spring Promo row. A 'Check facts against the export row' button shows three rows (primary_conversion page_view vs page_view, conversions 96 vs 96, cost 1860 vs 1860), each labelled with the text 'Matches'.

Step 5 of 6 - What a later run needs: show that no post-fix export exists. Show Brand's previous-period workbook row with formula text '=275/19', result '14.47', cost change '15' from formula text '=290-275', conversion change '3' from formula text '=22-19'. Show 'Search-terms export: not provided' under NEEDS YOUR CHECK. Show AI INTERPRETATION that a cost change of 15 is not a reason to move budget. Show the sentence 'Re-run after 14 days with a new campaign export. Do not change bids yet.'

Step 6 of 6 - You change it: state the exact sentences 'You change it in Google Ads. The kit changes nothing.' and 'Do not change bids yet.' Explain that the person sets form_submit as primary in Google Ads themselves, or decides not to, and that nothing is sent, edited, or paid automatically. Offer a link to the Premium kit labelled as private preview with sign-in required.

kit_contents.title: Google Ads Performance Setup Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Step-by-step setup for one review. It covers writing the qualified outcome, exporting current and previous Google Ads campaign CSVs with campaign, clicks, cost, conversions, primary_conversion, and each file's date range, capturing the conversion-actions screenshot from Goals > Conversions > Summary, exporting GA4 Traffic acquisition and Landing page reports for the same ranges, adding a search-terms export when the campaign type provides one, checking the AI tool's data settings before pasting or uploading, and the rule that this is an export review, not a live connector. It notes that file upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings, and that rows can be pasted as text instead.

kit_contents.title: Measurement Review Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt that runs the measurement check first, compares each primary_conversion to the owner's qualified outcome, writes MEASUREMENT REVIEW FIRST and stops efficiency ranking when the primary conversion is not qualified, labels CONFIRMED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately, and forbids bid, budget, status, or targeting changes, invented numbers, and editing the Google Ads account.

kit_contents.title: Period Review Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt used only after every in-scope campaign passes the measurement check. It fills the workbook from current and previous export numbers, leaves formulas visible, compares periods without inventing savings or ROI, and forbids bid or budget changes and any edit to the Google Ads account.

kit_contents.title: Qualified Outcome Worksheet
kit_contents.purpose: Browser-only form where the person writes the qualified outcome, confirms or turns off the default 'does not count' events, and lists campaigns to mark out of scope. It generates a copyable rules block to paste with the Measurement Review Prompt. Nothing is saved to Atlas.

kit_contents.title: Calculation Workbook Template
kit_contents.purpose: Column layout (campaign, period, clicks, cost, conversions, primary_conversion, formula, result, meaningful) with the fictional demo numbers and visible formula text such as =1860/96. Includes a Copy CSV button so the person can start their own spreadsheet. Spring Promo is labelled meaningful = no.

kit_contents.title: Action Review Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Interactive, session-only checklist used before changing anything in Google Ads. It confirms that the qualified outcome is written down, that MEASUREMENT REVIEW FIRST ran before efficiency ranking, that each CONFIRMED number matches an export row, that labels are separate, that no bid or budget change is recommended while measurement failed, and that the person will make any change in Google Ads themselves.

kit_contents.title: Fictional Sample Exports
kit_contents.purpose: The same fictional campaign, previous-period, conversion-action, and GA4 CSVs used in the guided demo, labelled as fictional, with a Copy CSV button. The person can practice the full workflow in their AI tool before using real account data.

kit_contents.title: Data and Safety Guidance
kit_contents.purpose: Rules for handling ad-account exports in AI tools: review data settings, remove unneeded columns, do not paste passwords or billing details, do not treat a GA4 All Users report as paid Google traffic, do not force Google Ads and GA4 counts to match, and do not change live bids from a hypothesis. It also states that file upload support differs by plan and that nothing is sent, edited, or paid automatically.

decision_rules: Use each export's own date range, not today's date. If a campaign export has no date range, ask the person for it before ranking anything.
Write MEASUREMENT REVIEW FIRST and apply it before any efficiency ranking, cost-per-conversion comparison, or bid or budget suggestion.
A campaign whose primary_conversion does not match the owner's qualified outcome is skipped for efficiency ranking. Show the reason 'primary conversion is not the qualified outcome'.

If the conversion-actions screenshot or table is missing, or a remaining row is missing campaign, cost, conversions, or primary_conversion, or the same campaign name appears twice in one period, do not rank it. List it under NEEDS YOUR CHECK.
Do not invent clicks, cost, conversions, sessions, events, savings, or ROI. Use only values from the files the person pasted.
Leave every workbook formula visible as text (for example =1860/96). AI must not hide the arithmetic or replace it with a rounded marketing figure.
A cost-per-conversion figure on a campaign that failed measurement may be shown only with meaningful = no and must not be used to rank spend or to recommend a bid or budget change.
Do not treat a Google Ads conversion count and a GA4 event count as the same metric. List both as CONFIRMED counts from their own exports. Any cause of a gap is AI INTERPRETATION.
Do not treat a GA4 All Users report as paid Google traffic. If the export is not filtered to paid Google, list it under NEEDS YOUR CHECK.
Search-terms are optional. If the file is missing, write 'Search-terms export: not provided' under NEEDS YOUR CHECK. Do not invent queries.
Skip any campaign the owner marked out of scope. Show the reason 'marked out of scope by you'.

Do not recommend bid, budget, status, or targeting changes while any in-scope campaign fails the measurement check. Allowed suggestions are verify tracking, set the qualified outcome as primary, wait, and re-export.
Never claim that spend was wasted, that a change will save money, or that a result is ROI. Period differences are calculations from the two exports, not savings claims.
AI INTERPRETATION must state that a failed measurement check means the conversion number is not a qualified outcome, not that the campaign is a proven waste of spend.
On a later run, use a new pair of exports. Do not invent a post-fix results file. If the person has not attached a new export, say that no new export was provided.
human_ai_boundary: AI compares each primary_conversion to the qualified outcome the owner wrote. The person defines that outcome and decides whether a page view ever counts.
AI writes MEASUREMENT REVIEW FIRST and stops efficiency ranking when measurement fails. The person decides whether to change tracking in Google Ads or to accept the current setup.
AI fills the workbook from export numbers and leaves formulas visible. The person checks every CONFIRMED number against the export row before treating it as true.
AI labels CONFIRMED facts, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. The person decides whether a hypothesis is worth investigating.

AI never connects to Google Ads or GA4, never changes a bid, budget, status, or targeting, and never uploads the person's files to a third party. The person makes every change in Google Ads, or decides not to.
AI reads only the files the person pasted. Only the person records what they changed in the live account.
The person decides whether any recommended action happens.
safety: Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically. Every page states that the person changes Google Ads themselves and that the kit changes nothing.
Atlas does not connect to Google Ads, GA4, Google Analytics, or any other vendor. It has no OAuth flow, no API call, and does not upload the person's data to any third party.

Before pasting or uploading exports to an AI tool, the person is told to review that tool's data settings (such as chat history, training use, and file retention) and to remove columns the workflow does not need.
The kit tells the person not to paste Google account passwords, billing account numbers, or customer emails into the AI tool.
File upload support and data controls in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini differ by plan, account, and admin settings. The kit says so and does not claim any plan includes a specific capability.
The kit tells the person not to change live bids, budgets, or campaign status from a hypothesis, and not to treat MEASUREMENT REVIEW FIRST as proof that spend was wasted.
Google Ads and GA4 counts are not forced to match. A gap is shown as two CONFIRMED export counts, not as a diagnosed tracking bug.
A GA4 All Users export is not treated as paid Google traffic.
All demo and sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional on the page.
Worksheet entries and checklist progress stay in the browser session only and are not saved to Atlas.
The pages contain no statistics, savings, ROI claims, prices, or checkout. Fictional campaign costs and workbook results are the only dollar figures.
required_data_tools: Google Ads campaign export (CSV) for the current period and the previous period, with campaign, clicks, cost, conversions, primary_conversion, and each file's date range
Conversion-actions screenshot or table from Google Ads Goals > Conversions > Summary
GA4 Traffic acquisition and Landing page exports for the same two periods
Search-terms export when the campaign type provides one
Spreadsheet (Google Sheets or Excel) so workbook formulas stay visible
A file-capable AI assistant. File upload support differs by plan, account, and admin settings; rows can be pasted as text instead.
